subject: CloudScope invoice INV-8891 — failed payment & VAT entity split request
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudscope.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Payment failed for INV-8891 (CloudScope) — can we split VAT to UK entity?

Hi Avery,

Stripe just notified us that the payment for invoice INV-8891 failed when our virtual card attempted authorization. Our billing team saw the decline code is `card_declined` from the acquirer. Can you re-attempt the charge, or alternatively reissue the invoice so we can pay by bank transfer?

Two asks:
- We need the invoice split so the VAT portion is billed to CloudScope UK Ltd (VAT ID: GB999888777) and the remainder to CloudScope Analytics (US). For compliance it needs separate VAT lines and a VAT registration number on the UK copy.
- If you can retry via Stripe one-time using the original invoice (we can provision a new card), that would be quickest. If retrying, please confirm whether the retry will incur duplicate invoicing or a credit memo.

I've attached our remittance stub for today (CloudScope_remittance_0920.pdf). Let me know the easiest path — reissue vs retry — and any form we need to fill for VAT split.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Finance | CloudScope Analytics
elena.ortiz@cloudscope.com
Attachment: CloudScope_remittance_0920.pdf

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudscope.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 12:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment failed for INV-8891 (CloudScope) — can we split VAT to UK entity?

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the remittance stub.

Short answers up front:
1) We can attempt a one-time retry against the existing invoice in Stripe if you provide a replacement card or approve a bank transfer. A retry will *not* create a duplicate invoice — if successful Stripe marks the invoice as paid. If retry fails again we'll follow normal retry and dunning policies and keep you posted.
2) We can reissue a new invoice split across entities (separate invoice numbers) so each shows the correct VAT registration number. That path is preferred for your auditors. Our finance team needs the exact legal name and VAT ID for each entity and confirmation of which line items map to the UK company.

Next steps I propose:
- Elena: confirm the legal name and VAT ID for the UK entity and which products/lines should be billed to which entity.
- Marcus: can you prepare a split invoicing option (two invoices: INV-8891-UK and INV-8891-US) and confirm whether we should void the original or put it into credit memo state?
- Monica: please hold off on retrying the card until we confirm — if they want bank transfer we should reissue and include wire instructions.

If you prefer we can also open a quick Stripe dispute-free retry (manual retry) — Marcus, Monica, I can sign off.

--
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com
Attachment: INV-8891.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudscope.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment failed for INV-8891 (CloudScope) — can we split VAT to UK entity?

Thanks Avery / Elena — looped in Finance ops for the reissue. Summary of internal decisions:
- We'll generate two invoices derived from INV-8891: INV-8891-UK (for CloudScope UK Ltd) and INV-8891-US (for CloudScope Analytics).
- The original INV-8891 will be moved to a credit memo (to avoid duplicate tax records) and will show zero balance after the split invoices are created.
- I'll create the UK invoice with the VAT ID GB999888777 and include the VAT line. The US invoice will be net amounts with no VAT.
- For payment methods: if CloudScope wants to retry via Stripe, we can do a single manual retry attempt after the customer provides a new card token or authorizes us to process the existing authorization. Otherwise, provide wire instructions and we'll mark the new invoices as unpaid until receipt.

Elena, quick confirmation required: please confirm the exact legal name as it should appear on INV-8891-UK and whether billing address should be the UK head office or the US office. Also confirm whether you want us to attempt the one-time Stripe retry after reissuing the split invoices.

I will attach a draft of the split invoices once generated for sign-off.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Finance Ops Analyst
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@cloudscope.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment failed for INV-8891 (CloudScope) — can we split VAT to UK entity?

Hi Marcus / Avery,

Thanks for the quick coordination. Confirming details:
- Legal name for UK invoice: CloudScope UK Ltd
- VAT ID: GB999888777
- Billing address for UK invoice: 14 Kingsway, London WC2B 6NH, United Kingdom
- Please map the platform subscription lines (items 1–3 on the original invoice) to the UK entity. Any professional services (item 4) should remain on the US invoice.

We prefer bank transfer for this one — please reissue the invoices and include your wire instructions. Once you reissue, I'll route for payment; attaching our remittance again for reference.

If you need anything else from our side (PO number or updated W-9/W-8), let me know.

Appreciate the help — Elena
